decks.name: LeetCode #207 - Course Schedule
decks.description: Determine if it's possible to finish all courses given prerequisites using cycle detection in directed graph

cards.question: Course Schedule: There are a total of numCourses courses you have to take, labeled from 0 to numCourses - 1. You are given an array prerequisites where prerequisites[i] = [a_i, b_i] indicates that you must take course b_i first if you want to take course a_i. For example, the pair [0, 1] indicates that to take course 0 you have to first take course 1. Return true if you can finish all courses. Otherwise, return false.

solutions.name: Cycle Detection (DFS)
solutions.explanation: Use DFS to detect cycles in prerequisite dependency graph. Build adjacency list mapping each course to its prerequisites. Use visiting set to track courses in current DFS path - if we revisit a course in current path, cycle detected. DFS returns false if cycle found, true if course can be completed. Mark completed courses by emptying their prerequisite list to avoid reprocessing. Remove course from visiting set after exploring all its prerequisites (backtrack). Run DFS on all courses. If any returns false, impossible to finish. This detects circular dependencies that prevent completion. Time O(V+E) visiting each course and prerequisite once. Space O(V+E) for adjacency list and recursion stack.

solutions.timeDescription: We visit each course (vertex) at most once and traverse each prerequisite edge once. Building adjacency list takes O(E), DFS visits all V vertices and E edges
solutions.spaceDescription: Adjacency list stores all E edges across V courses. Visiting set and recursion stack can hold up to V courses in worst case
solutions.exampleWalkthrough: Given numCourses=2, prerequisites=[[1,0]]: Build preMap: {0:[], 1:[0]}. DFS on course 0: no prerequisites, return true. DFS on course 1: prerequisites [0], DFS on 0 returns true, mark 1 as complete. All courses can be finished, return true. Example with cycle: prerequisites=[[1,0],[0,1]]: preMap={0:[1], 1:[0]}. DFS on course 0: add 0 to visiting, check prerequisite 1, DFS on 1 adds 1 to visiting, check prerequisite 0, but 0 already in visiting, cycle detected, return false.

solutions.name: Topological Sort (Kahn's Algorithm)
solutions.explanation: Use BFS-based topological sort with indegree tracking. Build adjacency list where edge from src to dst means src must be taken before dst. Track indegree (number of prerequisites) for each course. Initialize queue with all courses having zero prerequisites (indegree 0). Process queue: for each course, increment finish count and decrease indegree of dependent courses. When dependent course reaches indegree 0, add to queue. If we can finish all courses (finish equals numCourses), no cycle exists. If cycle exists, some courses will never reach indegree 0. This is Kahn's algorithm for topological sort. Time O(V+E) processing each course and edge once. Space O(V+E) for adjacency list and indegree array.

solutions.timeDescription: We process each course once when dequeued (V operations) and traverse each prerequisite edge once when updating indegrees (E operations)
solutions.spaceDescription: Adjacency list stores E edges across V courses. Indegree array stores V values. Queue can hold up to V courses
solutions.exampleWalkthrough: Given numCourses=4, prerequisites=[[1,0],[2,0],[3,1],[3,2]]: Build indegree=[0,1,1,2] and adj={0:[1,2], 1:[3], 2:[3], 3:[]}. Course 0 has indegree 0, start with queue=[0]. Process 0: finish=1, decrease indegree of neighbors 1 and 2 to [0,1,1,2]→[0,0,0,2], add 1 and 2 to queue. Process 1: finish=2, decrease indegree of 3 to 1. Process 2: finish=3, decrease indegree of 3 to 0, add 3 to queue. Process 3: finish=4. finish equals numCourses, return true. All courses can be completed in topological order: 0→1→2→3.
